title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
abstract: Rust crates confine unsafe code, such as calls into C or C++ libraries or system calls, behind safe interfaces that must uphold Rust's invariants. If an interface encodes one rule of the code beneath it too weakly, a program written in purely safe Rust can cause undefined behavior. Static analyzers and fuzzers are bound to fixed patterns or to the paths they execute. We propose LLM agents as auditors of these interfaces, and study how well they do it. We first define a taxonomy of the defects of such interfaces, including undefined behavior, divergences from the wrapped library, and incomplete unsafe contracts. We then measure, in repeated audits of a real-world crate by a closed and an open model, Claude Opus 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, which defect classes agents find, how well they triage them, and what makes them find more. Agents find the first two classes unprompted, but find few incomplete contracts even when asked. Their findings are almost always real, even without an independent reviewer, yet they lack triage discipline: they seldom confirm with a sanitizer, and they stop early. With the same guidance, the open model finds as many defects as the closed one at a quarter of the cost. We integrate these insights in Crustify, an agentic system for automating C-to-Rust tasks, and run it at scale. In 16 widely used crates, including the bindings to the C libraries OpenSSL, SQLite, libgit2, and libcurl and to the C++ engine V8, Crustify found 225 undefined-behavior bugs, 23 behavioral divergences, and 36 incomplete unsafe contracts, between 3 and 61 per crate at a median cost under $50 per audit. In the Linux kernel's Rust abstractions, it found 11 more undefined-behavior bugs and 4 incomplete contracts. Maintainers have fixed 26 of the 83 findings that we reported.
title_zh: 智能发现Safe Rust绑定中的健全性错误
abstract_zh: Rust crate将不安全代码（如调用C或C++库或系统调用）限制在必须维护Rust不变量的安全接口之后。如果接口对底层代码规则的编码过于薄弱，完全用安全Rust编写的程序可能导致未定义行为。静态分析器和模糊测试工具局限于固定模式或它们执行的路径。我们提出将大型语言模型(LLM)代理作为这些接口的审计者，并研究它们的审计效果。我们首先定义了此类接口缺陷的分类法，包括未定义行为、与被包装库的偏差以及不完整的不安全契约。然后，我们通过一个闭源模型(Claude Opus 5.5)和一个开源模型(DeepSeek V4.1 Flash)对真实世界的crate进行重复审计，测量它们发现的缺陷类别、分类能力以及发现更多缺陷的因素。代理能够主动发现前两类缺陷，但即使被要求，也很少发现不完整的契约。它们的发现几乎总是真实的，即使没有独立审查者，但缺乏分类纪律：它们很少使用sanitizer进行确认，并且会提前停止。在相同指导下，开源模型发现的缺陷数量与闭源模型相同，但成本仅为后者的四分之一。我们将这些见解整合到Crustify中，这是一个用于自动化C到Rust任务的代理系统，并在大规模运行。在16个广泛使用的crate中，包括对C库OpenSSL、SQLite、libgit2和libcurl的绑定以及对C++引擎V8的绑定，Crustify发现了225个未定义行为bug、23个行为偏差和36个不完整的不安全契约，每个crate发现3到61个问题，审计中位成本低于50美元。在Linux内核的Rust抽象层中，它发现了11个额外的未定义行为bug和4个不完整的契约。维护者已经修复了我们报告的83个发现中的26个。

title: Online Environment Repair for Coding Agents
authors: Sheng Lu, Rui Mao, Zewei Chen, Chihua Ying, Beiduo Chen, Dingxin Hu, Tinghao Yu
abstract: Programmatic verifiers provide scalable reward signals for training coding agents with reinforcement learning, yet subtle harness defects and incomplete unit tests allow policies to earn full credit without solving the intended task. Existing training-time defenses intervene either by penalizing suspicious outputs or by filtering flagged tasks and rollouts. However, output penalties leave the underlying verifier exploitable, driving policies to disguise shortcuts under reasoning monitors or zeroing out valid solutions under detector false positives, whereas task and rollout filtering discards or mutes the hardest problems where shortcuts emerge earliest. Pre-training verifier hardening repairs the environment directly, but misses vulnerability classes that surface only as the policy improves during reinforcement learning. In this paper, we propose online environment repair, which leaves triggering rollout rewards unchanged to remove hiding incentives and asynchronously patches exploited environments during training. Candidate repairs triggered by execution invariants or differential fuzzing are deployed only after passing three automated validation gates that block the exploit while preserving valid solutions, canceling detector false positives and enabling structural propagation across repositories without scaffold labels or reference solutions. Across 20 controlled GRPO experiments on heterogeneous software-engineering repositories, online environment repair reduces cumulative reward hacking from 36.9% to 0.06% and improves held-out Pass@8 from 21.7% to 46.7%, consistently outperforming reward-penalty, rollout-filtering, and static-hardening baselines while eliminating zero-shot exploitation on unseen loophole classes.
title_zh: 在线环境修复编程助手
abstract_zh: 程序化验证器为通过强化训练编码代理提供了可扩展的奖励信号，然而细微的验证器缺陷和不完整的单元测试允许策略在未解决预期任务的情况下获得满分。现有的训练时防御措施通过惩罚可疑输出或过滤标记的任务和轨迹来进行干预。然而，输出惩罚使底层验证器仍然存在可被利用的风险，导致策略在推理监控下伪装捷径，或在检测器出现误报时将有效解决方案归零；而任务和轨迹过滤则会丢弃或屏蔽出现捷径的最困难问题。预训练验证器加固直接修复环境，但错过了仅在强化学习过程中随着策略改进而出现的漏洞类别。在本文中，我们提出在线环境修复方法，该方法保持触发轨迹奖励不变以消除隐藏动机，并在训练期间异步修补被利用的环境。由执行不变性或差异模糊测试触发的候选修复仅在通过三个自动化验证门后才会部署，这些验证门能够阻止漏洞利用同时保留有效解决方案，消除检测器误报，并能够在没有支架标签或参考解决方案的情况下实现跨仓库的结构传播。在20个针对异构软件工程仓库的受控GRPO实验中，在线环境修复将累积奖励黑客行为从36.9%降至0.06%，并将保留的Pass@8从21.7%提高到46.7%， consistently优于奖励惩罚、轨迹过滤和静态加固基线方法，同时消除了对未见漏洞类别的零样本利用。

title: CPU-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models for CPU Hardware Code Generation
authors: Yuisei Iwata, Yutaka Masuda, Tohru Ishihara
abstract: Benchmarks such as VerilogEval have supported rapid advances in hardware description language (HDL) generation by large language models (LLMs). However, recent HDL-generation systems achieve pass rates above 90% on VerilogEval, leaving limited headroom for revealing further advances. To provide a challenging target for further progress on a practically important hardware-development task, we introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 HDL-generation problems constructed from six CPUs. Drawn from practical CPU designs, including families fabricated in silicon, the problems span CPUs from small embedded cores to Linux-capable out-of-order cores and cover diverse CPU functions written in SystemVerilog, Chisel, and SpinalHDL. In each problem, an LLM performs the real CPU-development task of generating HDL. Across seven state-of-the-art LLMs, mean pass@1 is 45.14 percentage points lower on CPU-Eval than on VerilogEval v2 Spec-to-RTL, exposing capability differences obscured by VerilogEval's high pass rates. CPU-Eval reveals that pass@1 is lower for submodules with more source-code lines, which motivates fine-grained modular design for LLM-aided hardware generation. We also show that pass@1 is lower for CPUs written in less widely used HDLs, motivating designers to verify that an LLM is sufficiently proficient at generating code in the HDL they use before deployment.
title_zh: CPU-Eval：评估大型语言模型在CPU硬件代码生成方面的能力
abstract_zh: 像VerilogEval这样的基准测试通过支持大型语言模型（LLM）快速推进硬件描述语言（HDL）的生成。然而，最近的HDL生成系统在VerilogEval上的通过率已超过90%，这为展示进一步进展留下了有限的空间。为了在具有重要实际意义的硬件开发任务上为进一步进展提供具有挑战性的目标，我们引入了CPU-Eval，这是一个由六个CPU构建的339个HDL生成问题基准测试。这些问题来源于实际的CPU设计，包括已在硅片中制造的系列CPU，涵盖了从小型嵌入式内核到支持Linux的无序执行内核，并使用了SystemVerilog、Chisel和SpinalHDL编写的多样化CPU功能。在每个问题中，LLM执行生成HDL的实际CPU开发任务。在七个最先进的LLM中，在CPU-Eval上的平均pass@1比在VerilogEval v2 Spec-to-RTL上低45.14个百分点，这揭示了VerilogEval高通过率所掩盖的能力差异。CPU-Eval显示，对于源代码行数更多的子模块，pass@1较低，这促使LLM辅助硬件生成采用细粒度模块化设计。我们还表明，对于使用不太常用的HDL编写的CPU，pass@1较低，这促使设计师在部署前验证LLM是否足够擅长生成他们所使用的HDL中的代码。
